lead: Chattanooga sits in a river valley ringed by ridges, where storms build fast and creeks rise quickly. Tornadoes, flash floods and crawl space moisture cause most of its water damage.
risk: tornado damage, flash flooding and crawl space moisture
why: On the night of April 12, 2020, an EF3 tornado tore through East Brainerd and other parts of Hamilton County. It damaged hundreds of homes, and many roofs were torn open in the rain. Spring storms bring wind and hail almost every year, and the ridges around the city funnel storms through the valley. Fallen trees are a common cause of roof leaks in wooded neighborhoods.

The Tennessee River once flooded downtown often, but TVA dams now hold it back. Creeks are the bigger risk today. Heavy rain runs off the ridges into Chattanooga Creek, South Chickamauga Creek and others, and low streets can flood within an hour. Many homes sit over crawl spaces, and the humid valley air keeps them damp. A small leak there can quickly lead to rot and mold.
image_alt: Workers repairing flashing around a brick chimney
image_caption: After storms, Chattanooga roofs and chimney flashing are sealed before drying starts.
problems: Homes near Chattanooga and South Chickamauga creeks
Older homes in Highland Park, St. Elmo
Crawl space drying and mold control
tips: Have a plan and a safe room for tornado warnings.
Trim limbs over the roof before storm season.
Add a vapor barrier and keep crawl space vents working.
Know if your home sits near a creek that floods.
areas: Calls come from the North Shore, Southside, St. Elmo, Highland Park, Riverview, Brainerd, Hixson and Lookout Valley, plus East Ridge, Red Bank and Signal Mountain.

faq.q: Does insurance cover crawl space mold in Chattanooga?
faq.a: Usually only if it comes from a sudden, covered leak, like a burst pipe. Mold from long-term humidity or slow seepage is often excluded. Some policies also cap mold coverage. Keeping the crawl space dry with a vapor barrier and good drainage is the best protection.
